transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: Totally hear you — if you spent three months and saw nothing, you *should* be skeptical.  

Before I answer why we’d be different, can you tell me what that agency was actually supposed to be doing for you — more calls, more booked jobs, ads, something else?
User: They promised to boost our call bookings significantly, but nothing changed after we signed up.
Agent: Yeah, that’s frustrating — you were sold “more booked calls” and just got more waiting.  

So if we *did* increase your call bookings, what would that actually mean for you — more new customers, better use of the team’s time, or just not feeling like the phone is going dead?
User: More new customers and better use of our team's time would make a big difference for us.
Agent: Got it, so this really comes down to: if calls turn into actual booked customers and your team isn’t wasting time, it’s a win.  

So I don’t over-assume — how are you handling incoming calls today when the phone rings and no one’s free to grab it?
User: We often miss calls because we're busy with patients, and those missed opportunities really add up.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — if you’re with patients, you *can’t* live on the phones, but those missed calls are still missed customers.  

When a call comes in right now and no one can pick up, does it usually roll to voicemail, ring out, or go to some kind of answering service?
User: It usually goes to voicemail, but we rarely get callbacks from that. It feels like lost opportunities.
Agent: Right, so calls hit voicemail, people don’t call back, and it just feels like money slipping away.  

Roughly how many calls a day or week would you say end up in voicemail instead of talking to a real person?
User: We miss about 18 calls a week, and most end up in voicemail without a callback. It's frustrating.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — 18 calls a week just dropping into voicemail is a *lot* of potential new patients slipping away.  

Given that, are you mainly looking for a way to turn those missed calls into booked appointments automatically, or is your priority freeing up your team’s time first?
User: Turning missed calls into appointments is the priority. But, I need to know this isn't just empty promises.
Agent: Totally fair — after what you went through, you shouldn’t take anyone’s word at face value.  

So… with those 18 missed calls a week, has anyone ever actually walked you through what that’s costing you in lost appointments?
User: Not exactly. I estimate, but no one's shown me a clear picture of the potential impact.
Agent: Makes sense — most people just feel the loss but never see the actual number.  

Mind if we do a super quick back-of-the-napkin calc together on those missed calls, just to see what you *might* be leaving on the table?
User: Sure, let's see what that looks like. But remember, I've been burned by vague promises before.
Agent: Totally get it — we’ll stick to your numbers, nothing fluffy.  

So ballpark, of those 18 missed calls a week, what percentage do you think would’ve actually booked an appointment if someone had picked up — maybe half, around 50%, or more like 30–40%?
User: I'd say about 60% would book if someone answered. But, how do I know you'll actually deliver?
Agent: Totally fair question — we’ll come back to “why we’re different” in a sec, and I’ll keep it concrete, not fluffy.  

First, to finish the picture: on average, what’s a new appointment worth to you in dollars — roughly what you collect from a typical first visit?
User: A typical first visit brings in about $240. But what happens after I sign up with you?
Agent: Using *your* numbers — 18 missed calls a week, 60% would book, $240 a visit — that’s about $2,591 a week in lost revenue… and roughly $11,200 a month walking out the door.  

So, if we could reliably turn a chunk of that into booked appointments without adding staff, would you want to dive into how our system actually handles those missed calls day-to-day?
User: That sounds promising, but what happens after I sign up? I've been let down by vendors before.
Agent: Totally get that — being burned before makes you want to know exactly what you’re walking into.  

So, the moment you sign up, what would make you feel “Okay, this is actually moving in the right direction” in the first 30 days — more booked appointments on the schedule, clearer reporting, or just seeing fewer calls hit voicemail?
User: More booked appointments and fewer calls hitting voicemail would be key. But will I get dropped once I pay?
Agent: Makes total sense to ask that — you don’t want another “pay and disappear” situation.  

So, here’s how we handle it: we don’t just run ads or hand you “leads”; we put a system on your phones that answers when you can’t, books the appointment right into your schedule, and then we review the call data with you so you can *see* how many of those 18 missed calls a week are actually turning into new patients — no guessing, just numbers.  

Given you’re leaking about $11,200 a month from missed calls, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how that works on your calls and what your numbers look like with it turned on — is later today or tomorrow better for you?
User: Okay... one demo. But remember, I'm watching closely. Tomorrow works. And stick to Mountain/Phoenix time.
Agent: Got it, we’ll keep everything on Mountain time and we’ll earn your trust, not assume it.  

To get that demo locked in, can I grab your first name?
User: Sure, it's Bianca. And remember, I'm only interested if this truly addresses our missed calls issue.
Agent: Thanks Bianca — and totally noted, this has to *actually* fix the missed calls, not just sound good.  

And what’s your last name, so I make sure the calendar invite is correct?
User: Cole. But again, I'm cautious. I need to see real results, not just hear promises.
Agent: Got it, Bianca Cole — and yeah, you should be cautious after your last experience.  

What’s the name of your practice so I can note it for the demo?
User: It's Cole Family Dental. Just make sure this demo shows how you handle missed calls effectively.
Agent: Perfect, Cole Family Dental — and yes, we’ll stay focused on how we turn those missed calls into booked appointments.  

Quick check, Bianca: is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to text your demo confirmation to?
User: Yes, it is. But remember, I'm expecting clear results and transparency with this demo. No fluff, just facts.
Agent: Totally with you — tomorrow’s demo will be straight numbers and call flows, no fluff.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as 9:45 am or 2:15 pm Mountain; which works better for you?
User: Let's do 2:15 pm Mountain. I'll be watching closely for everything you promised.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on the calendar.
Agent: Thanks Bianca. You’re all set for tomorrow at 2:15 pm Mountain with Jay for your Dialux demo. You’ll get a text with the confirmation and a link in case you need to reschedule. Before we hang up, is there anything else you need from me right now?
